reference: GNU coreutils ln, with exact stdout/status and private filesystem bytes, modes, hardlink relationships and symlink targets. Bash type/help checks are metadata contracts.
coverage: Hard links, relative and dangling symlinks, multiple operands, collisions, force replacement, spaced names and missing operands.
Single-operand destination, -- and dash names, symlink replacement, partial failure and repeated calls.
Bash registration and help metadata; separately identified from operations.
exclusions: Interactive prompting and filesystem fault injection are outside this bounded suite; no privileged operation is needed for ordinary links.

cases.purpose: Confirm Bash resolves ln as a builtin with the executable search path empty, using the documented type -t classification.
Confirm help exposes the documented short usage string registered for ln without invoking the loadable operation.
Create a hard link; compare bytes, modes, link count and inode relationship.
cases.script:
printf 'link bytes\n' > source
ln source destination
[[ source -ef destination ]]
stat -c '%h' source

cases.purpose: Preserve the relative symlink target and read through it from its parent directory.
cases.script:
mkdir data links
printf 'relative bytes\n' > data/item
ln -s ../data/item links/current
readlink links/current
cat links/current

cases.purpose: A dangling symbolic link succeeds and preserves its literal target.
cases.script:
ln -s future-name dangling
[[ -L dangling && ! -e dangling ]]
readlink dangling

cases.purpose: Create multiple relative symlinks into an existing directory and compare followed bytes and stored targets.
cases.script:
mkdir output
printf one > one
printf two > two
(cd output; ln -s ../one ../two .)
cat output/one output/two

cases.purpose: An existing destination is preserved on failure, including both original file payloads.
cases.script:
printf original > source
printf keep > destination
ln source destination

cases.purpose: Replace only the private destination with a hard link and compare its resulting tree.
cases.script:
printf original > source
printf replace > destination
ln -f source destination
[[ source -ef destination ]]

cases.purpose: Quoted operand boundaries survive hard-link creation.
cases.script:
printf bytes > 'source with space'
ln 'source with space' 'destination with space'
[[ 'source with space' -ef 'destination with space' ]]

cases.purpose: Compare missing-operand status and diagnostic presence without mutating the fixture.
A single source operand creates its basename in the current private directory.
cases.script:
mkdir origin dest
printf item > origin/item
(cd dest; ln ../origin/item)
[[ origin/item -ef dest/item ]]

cases.purpose: Use -- with a dash-leading source and replace a private dangling symlink with -sf.
cases.script:
printf x > -source
ln -- -source hard
ln -s stale symbolic
ln -sf -- -source symbolic
readlink symbolic

cases.purpose: Compare aggregate failure status and successful middle link amid two missing sources.
cases.script:
mkdir dest
printf x > good
ln absent good missing dest

cases.purpose: Compare ln hardlink/symlink effects within a private tree assembled with ordinary GNU file operations; also preserve bytes and modes through the surrounding copy/move/removal steps.
cases.script:
mkdir -p -- alpha/sub
printf 'fixture data\n' > alpha/sub/source
ln -- alpha/sub/source alpha/hard
ln -s -- sub/source alpha/symbolic
cp -- alpha/sub/source alpha/copy
chmod 640 alpha/copy
mv -- alpha/copy alpha/moved
touch -- alpha/stamp
touch -- alpha/remove-me
rm -- alpha/remove-me

cases.purpose: Compare ln hardlink/symlink effects within a private tree assembled with ordinary GNU file operations; also preserve bytes and modes through the surrounding copy/move/removal steps.
cases.script:
mkdir -p tree/src tree/dst
touch tree/src/original tree/to-remove
printf 'payload\n' > tree/src/original
chmod 640 tree/src/original
cp -p tree/src/original tree/copied
ln tree/src/original tree/hard
ln -s src/original tree/symbolic
mv tree/copied tree/dst/copied
rm tree/to-remove
touch tree/dst/touched
chmod 600 tree/dst/touched
printf 'fixture-ready\n'

cases.purpose: Compare ln hardlink/symlink effects within a private tree assembled with ordinary GNU file operations; also preserve bytes and modes through the surrounding copy/move/removal steps.
cases.script:
mkdir -p source/nested
printf 'one\n' > source/nested/item
cp -R source copied
mv copied moved
chmod 700 moved
rm -r source
printf 'recursive-fixture-ready\n'
ln moved/nested/item linked-item
[[ moved/nested/item -ef linked-item ]]

cases.purpose: The documented -n option replaces a symlink to a directory instead of following it when combined with -f.
cases.script:
mkdir target
printf data > source
ln -s target destination
ln -fn source destination
[[ source -ef destination && ! -L destination ]]
